verdict: The materials are right — the didone numerals, the hairline ledgers, the wine-on-cream two-voice chat — but the pages are stacked, not composed: Home queues five typographic events of near-equal weight down its top half and abandons the bottom 45% as leftover vacancy, which is the signature of an engineered screen wearing editorial type. The kept line, the supposed signature, is the palest ink on its own page, set smaller and fainter than the 860 below it and hemmed in by chrome (camera disc, hamburger, underline rule). The onboarding's courage — one thought per page, emptiness arranged around it — has not crossed over; only the chat page, bubble-less typeset correspondence, already reads as a publication. Verdict: engineered with taste, not yet designed.

compositions.composition: The daily front page. Top: 13pt letterspaced dateline alone (MONDAY, JULY 27 · DAY 12), no disc, no hamburger. Then the kept line as the headline of the day: 56–64pt cocoa JeniHeroSerif over two lines, flush left, the hollow ✦ seal sitting on the final baseline as terminal punctuation, one 15pt subline beneath. Then 180–220pt of true composed air. The lower half is one ledger, three rows, hairlines between: calories · 860 of ~1,473 / overnight fast · counts tomorrow / steps · 6,420 — labels 13pt left, values 34pt didone right. Bottom: word-only folio. One headline, one ledger, nothing else on the page.

The closing entry — a diary page, not a form. "closing the day." at 56pt. Below it the data absorbed into one typeset paragraph, 22pt serif on a 30pt leading: "protein 62 of 90g. tomorrow, a *balanced* day." Then the question "how did today feel?" in 17pt italic with the three bare words proud · okay · tender at 28pt serif spread across the full measure — the chosen one fills wine. Last: "best plate today?" in italic over a single bare baseline rule to write on. No boxes, no strokes, no section headers; four typographic moments descending in size like a letter signing off.

An issue cover, finally with an image. Her best plate photograph of the week runs full-bleed from the top edge to 55–60% height, square-cut, no corner radius; "becoming" sits over the photo's lower edge as a 15pt small-caps white masthead. On the cream below, the issue title at 64pt over two lines: "protein *earlier* in the day." with WEEK 2 OF 20 · FINDING STEADY as a 12pt folio line at the very foot. The cycle note becomes one wine 15pt line; "talk it through ↗" stays as the single italic footnote at 24pt. Fore-edge ticks live on the trailing edge, vertical, one per page. If no photo exists yet this week, the title scales to 76pt and owns the page alone — either an image event or a type event, never a half-page.

Unseen — all three captures show the cover frame, so this is composed from the brief. Rule for every interior spread: one figure, one sentence. The weight spread: the trend drawn as a single hairline cocoa curve across the FULL page width, no axes, no grid, no dots; where the line ends, the current weight at 96pt didone with its unit in 20pt italic; beneath, one 15pt caption ("down 1.1 kg across two weeks"). The pacing spread: the mounds figure enlarged to two-thirds page width, morning-to-night, with one 44pt serif claim above it and nothing else. Data drawn like a Fukasawa diagram, captioned like a plate in a monograph.

The correspondence — keep the grammar, dress the page. Masthead "jeni" drops to ~32pt italic; the dateline becomes a centered 12pt small-caps line between two short hairlines (— MONDAY, JULY 27 —), like a letter's dateline, replacing YOUR COACH · MONDAY and its colliding fragment. Each day's first message opens with its first line at 24pt serif (a salutation register) before settling to 19pt body; her lines stay wine, right-ragged, unbubbled. The input strips to a bare baseline rule with a small wine ↑; the duplicated exchange is purged. It is already the best page in the app — it just needs its margins pressed.

checklist_iconic.diagnosis: The kept line is styled as a section header among sections: the palest ink on the page, underlined like a form field, ornamented by a stray grey sparkle, upstaged by the 860 numeral below and the camera disc above. A signature must be the thing the eye lands on first and the hand touches last — nobody screenshots the quietest line on a screen, and nothing about it visibly invites an act.
checklist_iconic.proposal: The vow and the strike. One kept line per day set as the page headline — 56–64pt cocoa serif over two lines — with the hollow ✦ seal sitting on the final baseline as terminal punctuation. She holds the seal (the hold-to-build gesture from onboarding): the seal fills wine and a hairline draws itself through the whole line left to right, a pen crossing out a vow — trim-animated stroke, one soft haptic at completion. Kept days accumulate beneath as a ledger of struck-through 20pt lines, each ending in a filled seal, so by day 12 the page is a column of crossed-off vows under today's uncrossed one. That stack — today's loud unstruck line above yesterday's quiet struck ones — is the screenshot: a page that proves a practice. Buildable entirely with locked materials: JeniHeroSerif, cocoa/wine, one animated line, the existing ✦.

becoming_pageturn: Treat each page as a sheet, not a slide. Paging scroll with .scrollTargetBehavior(.paging) and a deliberately long settle; on each page use .scrollTransition to rotate the incoming sheet 4–6° around its leading edge (rotation3DEffect, anchor .leading) while scaling 0.985→1.0, so the leaf lifts and lays down; the outgoing sheet dims to ~96% brightness as ink settles. Interior parallax: the sheet moves at full speed but its headline offsets at ~0.94x, settling a beat after the page — type landing on paper. Edge treatment: at rest, 8–10pt of the next sheet peeks at the trailing edge behind a hairline shadow (a real fore-edge stack), and the dash stepper is replaced by vertical fore-edge ticks on the trailing margin, one hairline per page, the read ones tinted wine. After a page commits, its headline rises 12pt and fades in over ~320ms (the re-arm the pager already does), and the commit fires one soft haptic tick — the sound of a page falling, never a rubber-band bounce.
one_move: Invert Home's volume. Swap the scale of its two voices — the kept line up to 56–64pt full cocoa with the seal-and-strike ritual, the 860 down into a single 34pt ledger row — and strip the chrome around it (camera disc, hamburger, underline, stray sparkle) so the page is one headline, one ledger, and composed air. Home is the most-seen page and currently the most engineered; the moment its signature line actually leads it, every other surface's grammar (ledger rows, folio, correspondence) already agrees, and the app reads as a publication from the first screen.
